age.evidence: Male Wistar rats weighing 250 to 300 g were used.

sex.evidence: Male Wistar rats weighing 250 to 300 g were used.

dosing.evidence: Psilocin was prepared for intraperitoneal administration by dissolving the hydrochloride salt in saline. Systemic administration of a low dose of psilocin (1 mg/kg, i.p., n = 4)... Higher doses of psilocin (5 and 10 mg/kg, i.p., n = 5-6)

assays.assay_description: Rats placed in an observation cage (30 cm × 25 cm × 18 cm) immediately after psilocin administration; cumulative number of head twitches counted for 60 min by a blinded observer. Doses 1, 5, 10 mg/kg i.p.

setup_habituation.evidence: Rats were transferred to the testing room 30 min before testing. Immediately after psilocin administration, the rats were placed into an observation cage (no prior exposure to apparatus described).

setup_restrain.evidence: rats were placed into an observation cage (30 cm × 25 cm × 18 cm)

food_restriction.evidence: Rats placed into an observation cage with no mention of food access during the 60-min test.

water_restriction.evidence: Rats placed into an observation cage with no mention of water access during the 60-min test.

time_to_assay.evidence: Immediately after psilocin administration, the rats were placed into an observation cage

sample_size.evidence: Systemic administration of a low dose of psilocin (1 mg/kg, i.p., n = 4)... Higher doses of psilocin (5 and 10 mg/kg, i.p., n = 5-6)

outcomes.summary: Psilocin (10 mg/kg, i.p.) significantly increased the number of head twitches during a 60-min observation period, while 1 mg/kg had no effect on behaviour. The effect appeared dose-dependent.
outcomes.statistics: ** p < 0.01 vs. saline-treated group (Dunnett's multiple comparison test)
outcomes.evidence: Psilocin (10 mg/kg, n = 5) significantly increased the number of head twitches during a 60-min observation period.

B1_num_measures.evidence: the cumulative number of head twitches was counted for 60 min

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Data are expressed as the means ± S.E.M. (bars) and as the number of head twitches during a 20-min period

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of transitions or sequences reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Head-twitch response is treated as a hallucinogen-related readout, not an ethological behaviour per rubric.

B5_social.evidence: Single rat tested alone in observation cage.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: counted for 60 min by an observer blinded to the study protocol

E2_shelter.evidence: Plain observation cage with no enclosed refuge described.

E3_bedding.evidence: not reported; test cage thoroughly cleaned between animals

E6_spatial.evidence: observation cage (30 cm × 25 cm × 18 cm) - single compartment

E7_social_context.evidence: the rats were placed into an observation cage (one animal per session)

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in observation cage during the 60-min test.

D1_continuity.evidence: the cumulative number of head twitches was counted for 60 min

D4_baseline.evidence: Immediately after psilocin administration, the rats were placed into an observation cage (no pre-drug baseline).

judge_notes: All three candidates identified a single behavioural assay (Head-Twitch Test); microdialysis/HPLC measurements are neurochemical, not behavioural, so excluded per rubric.
B2 temporal dynamics: scored Yes because Figure 1 reports head twitches in 20-min bins within the 60-min session (within-session time course), agreeing with qwen and overriding gptoss/glm.
setup_habituation: scored 'no' rather than 'yes' (glm) — transfer to testing room 30 min before testing is room acclimation, not apparatus habituation, per rubric.
Housing conditions and several environmental items genuinely not reported; kept as not_reported/low confidence.
